COJ Billing Blunders

By: Johann Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
One year on has the COJ billing crisis been resolved?

Unique Selling Point:
CoJ has had a new government for the past 9 months. They inherited a system where the infrastructure is on the verge of collapsing due to years of abuse and non-maintenance. To fix the problems they claim that they need R170billion, yet they only have R10billion. And yet, their main source of income, the payment of rates, taxes and basic services is in total chaos. The billing crisis in itself is now a decade old, and there still seems to be very little if any progress made in resolving the thousands of disputes between the council and the residents. In our investigation, we start at the bottom with case studies who have no option but to pay bribes to get water and electricity, and we take it all the way to the top (the mmc for infrastructure, the mayor etc) to try and get to the bottom of this crisis

Summary:
It's more than a year since our last story on this topic. During this time not one of the case studies' billing problems have been solved. And thousands of new disputes have been lodged. People getting wrong accounts, often running into millions of rands, face monthly cut offs of both water and electricity, unable to pay the exorbitant amounts the council claims they owe. To date, the council has lost every single case that went to court, and this in itself costs the residents millions. Problems include faulty meters, wrong meter numbers, months of estimated readings in stead of actual readings, prescribed and inherited debt issues, and large scale corruption spanning the spectrum from meter readers to those working in the billing department. Frustration amongst residents is at an all time high, and at the same time the council is getting less and less money coming in.

Press Release:


COJ Billing Blunders
For over a decade, the City of Johannesburg’s rates, water and electricity billing system has been in absolute chaos. Exaggerated estimates, incorrect readings and system
errors have plagued residents and even though the city is under a new dispensation, it seems little has changed. It’s just over a year since Carte Blanche covered this
story. We follow up to find out whether any of the billing disputes featured, have in fact been resolved.

Script:


Water meter being stolen
How difficult is it to steal a water meter? – _-_-_-_
In broad daylight in a few seconds, the meter is gone. For the thieves, it's worth a few bob, but for the house owner it could be just the beginning of his troubles. No water for days and billing issues that could take years to resolve
Link Thuso
The Joburg billing crisis has been around for at least a decade, and yet still they receive up to 15000 new complaints every month. Now, for residents it can go from mild irritation to inconvenience to destroyed businesses and livelihoods.

In January last year we were told that the billing issues would soon be a thing of the past, but with the DA administration in charge of City Hall for 9 months now, they have finally admitted that this is far from true.
MMC Da GADA
When we arrived we bought into the spin by the officials. They said MMC, mr Mayor, don't talk about billing crisis, we have some glitches. But 9 months now in the job, the best way of describing it is Crisis

According to the municipality records Yvonne Botha ceased to exist after they installed a faulty prepaid meter more than a decade ago
UPSOUND
They said they'll send the people out and I've been waiting now for 12 years for them to come out.
Case study Mevrou Botha
Living on a R1500/month government grant, just getting to Braamfontein to ask for help is difficult. But despite various trips to Thuso House through the years, she's had no luck - COJ has no record of the meter or her account... and so she remains stuck with no power. She's had no option but to get someone to illegally bypass the meter. Now the plugs keep on burning out...
UPSOUND
I'm worried, because I'm scared I'll come home and my flat has burnt down. Because of this...

Jan and Berta have exactly the opposite problem – despite Bertha being registered on the Extended Social grant system, and so qualifying for vastly reduced rates and almost free water and electricity, she can't get the account transferred from her deceased mother’s name to her own - the system refuses to accept that her mother had passed away. Even submitting the death certificate didn't help
Case study Oom Jan
Hulle wil met mevrou A E Vos praat, en ons kannie Mev A E Vos vir hulle bring nie. Hulle kan miskien gaan kyk waar sy nou bly maar dis nie meer bo-grond nie.

The account, which was up to date at the time of her mother’s passing kept on increasing every month. And a year ago their electricity was summarily cut off
Oom Jan
Ons kry by ons bure, kry ons elektrisiteit. Hulle is op 'n prepaid. Hulle weet dis die bedrag wat hulle koop in 'n maand vir hulle self en vir alles wat oor dit gaan, die betaal Berta en ek.

Next their water was cut off, which according to attorney Chantelle Gladwin-Wood is illegal... for now...
Chantall
All residential households are entitled to 6 free kilolitres, so the city can't stop that supply lawfully – but that's gonna change on the first of July, because the tarriffs from the first of July onwards dont provide for that free water.
V/o
MMC Dagada denies that they would ever cut off water deliberately
MMC
R: Yes, we're not supposed to cut off. It could mean that uh some employee or the company that we've outsourced the service to didn't do what they supposed to be done
B: Well, it's illegal, it's a human rights issue.
R: Agreed.

Yet we have a list of people whose water has been cut off, implying that it is more than just a once-off mistake. And once again, Jan and Berta's neighbours are helping them survive with a hosepipe over the wall.
Oom Jan
So ook met hulle waterrekening wat hulle kry. Dit wat hulle nou gewoond was aan, dit wat nou meer is, die betaal ons

By law household electricity meters have to be physically read every 90 days and commercial meters every 30 days. But in reality this rarely happens and the constant high estimated readings add to the problem. Often when an actual reading is eventually done, the computer system refuses to accept it because it varies too much from the estimates.
MMC
If you are consuming around R2000, it can't be in the fourth month all of a sudden you are consuming R50 000. It's thumb suck numbers, that's all

Once you've logged a query they are not supposed disconnect you until it is resolved. But after 30 days the system automatically erases the query
Chantelle
How can you work in a system when you're query falls of the system in 30 days. It nol longer protects you from termination and the city doesnt even know that there is anything wrong any more.

Like thousands of residents, accountant Soso Gwadiso's meter was not read for several months. He lodged complaint after complaint about the exorbitant estimated readings and kept on paying his own estimate of what he owed.
Soso
So then we just started paying R3000 a month, R3000 a month until they sorted it out. Well...what we thought was sorted out.

While he was overseas on a business trip, his electrcity was suddenly disconnected. His wife, who has a little baby, went to the council and paid the entire amount under dispute in her desperation to get the electricity back on
Soso
So they allowed her to pay. And what was more frustrating is once she finished paying the full amount, then they said no, we can't connect you because the account is not in your name.

In the end it was all resolved, except it seems Soso could be in for a long fight to get the money he knows they owe him, back...
Dagada
The requirement that the customer must pay immediately or pay 50% is not there anymore. Actually it's not even in our by-law





This deserted building in Berea was bought by Mike Lingwood 9 years ago. 5 years before that all services to the building were terminated. Yet, when we interviewed him last year, they were still billing him for consumption and he owed millions, stopping him from fixing up the building.

15months later, nothing has changed. He is still billed monthly and the total account is now at over R7million
Mike
On a monthly basis they are charging us R41000 a month for water that is not going through that meter

Mike has no trust in the new MMC for finance
Mike
I don't blame the council officials in the call centre anymore, I personally hold the mmc for finance responsible in this case, because I have sat in a boardroom and I have given this to him and he assured us it would be fixed. This was part of 260 accounts that we gave to the mmc and the majority of them havent been fixed.

The MMC disagrees
Dagada
Most of those queries had been dealt with and I should also say this – amongst some of those queries, the city was on the right. There were those that were actually supposed to be paid. But our biggest weakness also is credibility, so even if somebody indeed, the city's on the right, they're supposed to pay – but because we don't have credibility, they can get away with it in terms of gaining sympathy.

Chantelle says it is even more difficult to resolve issues under the new administration
Chantall
We have seen a marked decrease in the help that we are able to get from the top levels in the city, and I can only presume what that is from, and that's from a fear that they will be seen by the new administration as being fraudulent when they write off money on a bill

Carlos Simoes, another of our 2016 case studies certainly experienced something similar. For the past five years his meter numbers and readings on his account haven’t matched that of his real meter or consumption. Despite keeping meticulous records and paying accordingly, his issue remains unresolved, with constant threats of disconnection, even after a senior official had come out to verify the validity of his complaint
Carlos
She sent a lot of emails out to different people, she organised for the meter readers to come here again, three times, different ones, came here. They all came here, confirmed my reading, confirmed my meter number, went back. The next month the invoicing is still the same. So nothing has happened.

B: This problem has been around for more than ten years, why is it not being fixed?
DG: Many years ago, around 2000, 16 councils were amalgamated into one metropolitan city, which is Johannesburg. And when they did that, they didn't clean up the data, when they brought in information technology. And later on this metro, implemented SAP, which is an information system, again without cleaning the data and huess what? As i'm talking to you now we were just about to upgrade this SAP, without cleaning the data
Chantelle
Until people at joburg understand how their own systems work, and are able to advise the general public of that, you're not going to get anywhere – you'r not going to fix anything
Mike
We are sick and tired of their excuses – it's very simple, all they must do is remove all the debt that is older than 3 years that shouldn't legally be on the accounts, and on a monthly basis make sure that their meters get read.

B: Can you at least promise us, here and now, on the record that at least the people that we have used to highlight these problems, you will sort it out?
DG: Uhm, I'm promising i'm going to attend to those queries personally. I'll deal with them
B: So by when will the prescribed debts be off the books?
DG: By end of August, by end of August. August this year
B: So you're putting your head on the block?
DG: You know what I said to the councillors and the mayor? If by the end of march next year, we haven't substantially reduced the billing crisis, so there musnt be billing crisis any more. If it is still there, I said to the mayor, dont even bother to fire me, I will leave



Promo1
Have you ever tried to get a faulty pre-paid meter repaired?
Upsound: 12 years
Why can't the city of joburg fix their decade long billing crisis


Promo2
Thousands of Joburg residents have been struggling for years to sort out their billing issues with the municipality
Mike: We are sick and tired of their excuses. It's very simple
Will the new administration fix the billing crisis?
